articles.title: Asus ROG Swift OLED PG27UCWM Review
articles.summary: The Asus ROG Swift OLED PG27UCWM offers a gorgeous display that works as well for cinematic games as it does for competitive, fast-paced ones.
body: Asus didn’t leave much out when it designed the ROG Swift OLED PG27UCWM. That said, it doesn’t have speakers, but you’ll find it checks boxes in just about every other department.

The PG27UCWM is ready for a lot of cables, too. You’ll find two HDMI 2.1 ports, a DisplayPort 2.1a port, and even a capable USB-C port that’ll take in video and send out up to 90 watts of power. There are two USB ports for passing data to a connected system, letting the monitor serve as a USB hub as well with a KVM switch so you can pass that connection to the USB-C link or a separate USB-B link. If you want to connect speakers, there’s a headphone jack, too.

Around back, the PG27UCWM spices things up a little. Rather than the classic black ABS plastic you’ll find on half the monitors in the world, the PG27UCWM opts for a transparent plastic that gives it something of a cyberpunk aesthetic. It may still feel like cheap plastic, but it looks damn good.

Another feature is a presence sensor that can help preserve the lifespan of the OLED panel by dimming it whenever you step away. I didn’t find it overly sensitive, so I wasn’t concerned it’d blink off while I’m in the middle of a game.
points: The Asus ROG Swift OLED PG27UCWM offers a gorgeous display that works as well for cinematic games as it does for competitive, fast-paced ones.

The character was originally played by William Campbell in the 1967 Star Trek episode “The Squire of Gothos,” where he treated the crew of the…
body: Trelane returns in Strange New Worlds season 4 to meddle with the Enterprise again, though this time in a more official capacity. In the episode "Like Chronitons Through the Hourglass," he does a school project with the thesis that “space adventures leave little time for humans to deal with their inner struggles.” He remedies that by trapping the crew in a soap opera — even changing the lighting and music — to force them to confront exaggerated versions of their problems. Polygon spoke with Darby about his role on the show and where else he’d like to cause some chaos.

“He's not quite as mischievous as he was,” Darby tells Polygon. “He's not being a cheeky trickster this time. He's actually doing something for his education. He's a little bit more mature. He gets to face Captain Pike and chat with him about how he sees humanity. He's taking it in a bit more. He still feels that they're just like ants, but they're ants that have got funny little brains and emotions that might help and might get in the way sometimes.”

articles.title: Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis Could Be Great, But There's Some Things We Can't Ignore...
articles.summary: Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis shows massive potential, but controversial changes like skill trees and modern hand-holding threaten to frustrate fans. And some of that food looks very suspicious.
body: The first thing that strikes you upon seeing the new Tomb Raider live-demoed on a massive 115” TV mere inches from your face, I can attest, is its visual fidelity: Legacy of Atlantis is absurdly pretty. Crammed with fine detail enough that every particle of dust and bat guano flitting through the stale air poses danger to your airways, it almost feels like it’s supposed to be funny when compared to the chunky textures and pointy polygons of the 32-bit original.

The game’s director Raul Siqueira puts it nicely during our session: “the secret to a good remake is knowing what to change, and what to leave well alone”. Absolutely. Preserving the essence of a thing is much more vital than slavishly recreating the original work, and this is certainly something that Legacy of Atlantis understands, aesthetically at least. It is unmistakably a modern interpretation of Lara Croft’s seminal adventure, an essential piece of gaming history arguably as important as Super Mario Bros. or Chuckie Egg (ask your dad).
points: Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis shows massive potential, but controversial changes like skill trees and modern hand-holding threaten to frustrate fans.

articles.title: Before HBO’s The Last Of Us, An Entirely Different Adaptation Was Proposed
articles.summary: Naughty Dog's first effort to adapt The Last of Us for the screen was not as an HBO TV show, but a movie, a fact that recently began doing the rounds again on social media.
body: While not everyone agrees with the creative departures from the source material for the TV series on HBO, it's undeniably a success and one of HBO's biggest hits lately. Let's look back at how The Last of Us originated as a movie and run through the key developments that led to it becoming a TV show.
People across X recently discovered a post from Sony Pictures in 2014 declaring that The Last of Us was "soon to be a major motion picture."

This was a real, studio-sponsored image, not a fan mock-up. There was officially produced key art, showing Ellie wielding a knife. There was a "secret panel" at San Diego Comic-Con that year featuring director Sam Raimi, who was originally attached to produce the movie, having already had huge success at Sony with his Spider-Man films.
That The Last of Us was originally going to be a movie is not surprising given how many video game movies came before it and how many have been released since (with varying degrees of success).

articles.title: Amazon Just Canceled The Most Subversive Spider-Man Show Ever Made
articles.summary: A new report has confirmed that Spider-Noir will not be getting a second season on Prime Video. While it is not continuing, another Marvel television show produced by Sony might see the light of day on the streaming platform.
body: Deadline revealed the cancellation in a Sept. 4 report, although Amazon did not give a specific reason as to why that happened. Deadline pointed out that while Spider-Noir had a strong debut, it dropped off Prime Video's top ten daily rankings faster than other popular shows like Reacher.

That said, Amazon does not appear to be completely displeased with how the show performed, as it is apparently still interested in making more series based on Spider-Man characters that Sony has adaptation rights to. While a series based on Silk got scrapped, Deadline claims that Amazon and Sony are developing "multiple projects" together, including one for an unspecified character that's "nearing a series order."

Spider-Noir was a very weird series, so I'm not actually surprised it didn't get a second season. It's a superhero action drama with a 62-year-old lead based on his portrayal of a Spider-Man variant in Into the Spider-Verse. Prime Video let viewers watch the series in both black-and-white and color, doubling the post-production work, and featured very different interpretations of classic Spider-Man villains like Sandman, Tombstone, and Black Cat.

articles.title: Gamescom apologises for how it initially responded to indie developer hardware thefts
articles.summary: Gamescom has apologised for the way it "communicated about the theft of hardware belonging to several indie developers" last week, admitting, "our first response did not strike the right tone, and it did not show the people affected the empathy they deserved".
body: Multiple exhibitors at Gamescom reported thefts of laptops and other equipment from their booths in Cologne last week, with one indie developer, Ryan Laley, saying the loss has effectively ended his show early. Iam8bit also reported two of its laptops were taken overnight from the same business area, as did Tessera Studios.
Addressing the thefts at the time, Gamescom said it was "aware of stolen hardware" and understood "the frustration of affected exhibitors", triggering further condemnation from attendees.

Now, in a new statement posted yesterday (4th September), Gamescom posted a follow-up statement on social media, saying the organisers "understand what this has cost you, and we should have said so from the very first moment".

A theft like this is far more than a material loss. It can ruin an entire Gamescom for the people it happens to, and it can destroy work that took months or years to build - work that, for a small studio, can be almost everything. To everyone affected: we understand what this has cost you, and we should have said so from the very first moment.

articles.title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword Has the Best Parry in Video Games
articles.summary: I’ll be honest: I’m sick of parrying in video games. What once was a unique combat mechanic has become as standard as jumping in action games. Even James Bond can parry in 007 First Light, as if he’s a Tarnished warrior taking down Radahn.
body: Capcom’s new action RPG, released Sept. 4 for consoles and Windows PC, follows the industry trends to create a combat system built around blocks, evasive dodges, and, yes, parries. It doesn’t sound all too interesting on paper, but Way of the Sword is a reminder that great animation and sound design can make a huge difference in a game. You can see that reflected in its parries, which are the finest counter-attacks I’ve ever felt in a game.

Way of the Sword ’s action is built entirely around reaction. As a skilled swordsman, Miyamoto Musashi knows how to read an opponent’s every move and respond with a deadly answer. Reflex dodges, Issen strikes, and blade locks all make you feel like you have mastered the art of the duel. You can always turn an enemy’s attack around on them if your timing is right, and you know the right move for every situation.
points: I’ll be honest: I’m sick of parrying in video games.

articles.title: BioWare doesn't need advice for Mass Effect 4, says veteran designer, as long as "people get out of the way"
articles.summary: Original Mass Effect cinematic designer and Mass Effect 2 lead cinematic designer Armando Troisi has insisted the current BioWare team doesn't need outside advice on developing the next installment because so many of the people who built the original trilogy are still at the studio.
body: Asked what guidance they'd offer developers working on the new game, Troisi didn't think they had anything to add.

"It's hard for me to say because a lot of people that are on that project were there [during the originals]," Troisi told FRVR. "They know. Preston [Watamaniuk] is there, and Derek [Watts] is there, and Parish [Ley] is there, and they're the OGs, you know? I don't think there's anything that I could tell them that they don't know what to do."
Troisi left the studio after Mass Effect 2, but has confident in the team that remains behind.

"When I was leaving, everybody wrote on a card… he [Preston] said, 'passion and craft is excellence'… I think they've got both of those so I don't think that I can give them any more advice than they already have. They know this stuff," Troisi said.

articles.title: Half of France's premier FPS sibling duo just put out the most exhilarating parkour game I've ever played, and it's only $8
articles.summary: Weird Weekend. Weird Weekend is our regular Saturday column where we celebrate PC gaming oddities: peculiar games, strange bits of trivia, forgotten history. Pop back every weekend to find out what Jeremy, Josh, Ted, and Rick have become obsessed with this time, whether it's the canon height of…
body: Vholume is not big on waypoints or barriers, and I love it for that. In the first level, there's a naturalistic, reasonably signposted "correct" path to walk you through the tutorial. I immediately went the opposite direction for shiggles to indulge my well-honed sense of childlike wonder and curiosity. I lost myself in a field of brutalist rooftops, wallrunning and mantling about with no sign of the beaten path in sight. I accidentally stumbled across the level secret this way, unlocking a B-side bonus mission.

My wanderlust eventually intersected with the critical path, and after wrapping the tutorial, I unlocked time trial mode for this level. After my super-chill freeform exploration, white knuckling it to a gold level time almost felt like a completely different game.

Alongside co-developers Nathan Grange and Niels Tiercelin, Vholume was created by Léonard Lemaitre, one half of the brotherly duo behind our 2024 FPS of the year, Straftat. This previous work was an atomically pure arena shooter, like Quake 3 by way of the Source engine. It was all about lightning-quick rounds and movement mastery, with a dry, slapstick sense of humor.

articles.title: Gen-AI controversy aside, Crazy Taxi: World Tour feels like classic arcade Sega - and it's an absolute blast
articles.summary: Crazy Taxi was not my favourite Dreamcast game (please don't ask me to choose between the triumphant rhythm triptych of Rez, Space Channel 5, and Samba de Amigo, however), but there's a specific bit of it that's forever seared into my brain: the giddy thrill of cresting over that one…
body: As a moment, it's the kind of perfect melding of style and blissful arcade purity that seemed to define so much of Sega's Dreamcast-era output. And my recent half-hour hands-on with the upcoming Crazy Taxi: World Tour at Gamescom suggests the original's 90s skate-punk spirit and taut arcade thrills are - if perhaps not equal - alive and well in this, Sega's long-awaited revival.

Crazy Taxi poster boy Axel is back (hair still green, shirt still Hawaiian, attitude less abrasive, and six pack now demurely hidden), as is the music of The Offspring and Bad Religion. Meaning that in terms of pure vibes, World Tour feels a lot like 1999 never left.

articles.title: White House launches Arcade.gov, a minigame site parodying immigration enforcement and border security
articles.summary: The White House has launched Arcade.Gov, a website of browser minigames built around Donald Trump's immigration and border policies.
body: As spotted by IGN, the site includes mini-games based on games like Flappy Bird.
A snake-like game called Rio Run wants you to collect a chain of prisoners in orange jumpsuits, tallying a "deported" count at the end of each run.

Other games on the site include Build the Wall: Zombie Border Siege, a Tetris riff where players stack bricks against incoming "aliens" at the "Southern Border", and Trump Savings Tycoon, which has a Washington DC backdrop and a falling-object catching mechanic, with memecoins and cash standing in for the usual coins or fruit, all in service of the game's stated goal to "fill your kids' Trump Accounts".
In a tweet, the administration wrote: "Build the wall. Deport. Fill a Trump Account".

articles.title: Gaming monitors are one of the only good things about PC hardware right now, but one niche feature is underloved
articles.summary: James is a more recent PC gaming convert, often admiring graphics cards, cases, and motherboards from afar. It was not until 2019, after just finishing a degree in law and media, that they decided to throw out the last few years of education, build their PC, and start writing about gaming…
body: The memory crisis may be in full swing, taking numerous PC components with it, but the value of gaming monitors is one of a few hardware things that has actually improved over the last few years. In fact, their price-to-quality ratio is kind of outrageous right now, with even relatively recent QD-OLED screens going for around $300.

As such, monitors are one of the few things I check over without rolling my eyes, and therefore, they're one of a handful of techie bits that actually excites me. But that doesn't mean even they can't improve; when I chatted to gaming monitor brand AOC a few months ago, even its designers are aware the software isn't up to snuff.

I've been testing out the Koorui G2741L, a dual mode 4K/1080p monitor, over the last few weeks, and all I can think is 'gosh, why aren't more companies doing dual mode,' and 'why aren't more companies doing dual mode better?'

One of these is the addition of vehicle refuelling, which will require players to stop off at gas stations (or petrol stations if you're a Brit like…
body: This mechanical tweak has proved somewhat controversial among Grand Theft Auto players, with some believing that refuelling cars will be inconvenient and interrupt the flow of driving and shooting the series is built upon. Yet while Rockstar is sticking to its guns on the matter of refuelling co-studio head Rob Nelson recently stated that filling up your car won't be a massive drag on your adventure across Vice City.

Nelson's comments come via YouTuber TGG (via GamesRadar+ ) who recently saw an extended preview of Rockstar's hotly anticipated crime sim, which included refuelling in action. TGG says that gas stations allow players to both repair and refuel cars, and facilitate recharging for electric vehicles alongside refuelling for cars powered by internal combustion engines. Selecting the refuel/recharge option triggers a refuelling cutscene that TGG says lasts around 10 seconds.
